subject: Monitoring hooks & SDK architecture — follow-up + questions
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Molly Chen <mchen@skylinehealth.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Monitoring hooks & SDK architecture — follow-up + questions

Hi Molly / Arjun,

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about Skyline's use of embeddings for patient record search and the reranker you plan to insert post-embedding. I wanted to capture the technical items we promised to follow up on and a few quick questions so Sergio and I can prepare the deep-dive.

Summary from our side:
- Primary use: semantic search + reranker for clinical notes (embedding + sparse hybrid).
- Traffic: ~200 qps at peak, mostly short queries (avg tokens per request ~120).
- Auth pattern: internal services call our API via Kong gateway.

Questions / asks (can you confirm?):
1) Trace propagation: do you currently carry a trace-id header (X-Trace-Id / x-request-id) through Kong into backend services? If so, what header name do you prefer for us to accept and echo?
2) Logs & fields: which log fields are most important for you to join traces to request metadata? (e.g., patient_id hash, request_id, route_name) — we can emit custom fields at token-level and request-level.
3) Latency breakdown: would you like per-hop headers (x-rw-latency, x-rw-kv-latency, x-rw-model-latency) or a single structured header with JSON?
4) Auth: are you using signed service-to-service JWTs today or API key + mTLS? Any requirement for rotating keys via your KMS?
5) Embeddings / reranker: will the reranker live in your stack (recommended) or in a Redwood pipeline? If in your stack, do you need a signed response proof to validate model outputs?

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Share a short SDK quickstart and an example middleware snippet for injecting / propagating trace IDs (attached).
- Sergio to run a 60-min technical deep-dive early next week focusing on auth + routing + header compatibility.
- Draft mapping of log/trace fields so we can align on dashboard joins.

Attachments included: sdk_auth_quickstart.pdf (quickstart + middleware examples), sample trace-field mapping.

Would you be available Wednesday or Thursday (PST) for the deep-dive? I can loop Jordan in for commercial context.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0132

From: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@skylinehealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Molly Chen <mchen@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Monitoring hooks & SDK architecture — follow-up + questions

Hey Camila,

Great summary — thanks. Quick answers below so you and Sergio can prep.

1) Trace propagation: we currently use x-request-id internally and forward it through Kong as X-Request-Id. We also have Datadog APM enabled; traces are linked with dd.trace_id. If Redwood can accept both x-request-id and x-rw-trace-id (and echo whichever we send) that'd be ideal.
2) Log fields: patient_id_hashed, request_id, route_env (prod/stage), and model_variant are the ones we join on. We can share our log schema — attaching a CSV with our current trace->field mapping. (attachment: trace-field-mapping.csv)
3) Latency headers: we'd prefer discrete headers per component (x-rw-client-latency, x-rw-routing-latency, x-rw-model-latency) — easier to parse into our dashboards.
4) Auth: currently API key between services, rotating monthly with our in-house KMS. We're experimenting with mTLS but not rolled out everywhere. For the POC, API key is fine.
5) Reranker: the reranker will sit in our infra after you return embeddings. We will call embeddings endpoint and then run our reranker. We may want a signed token or nonce included in the response to guard against replay — can you support a lightweight signed response header?

Availability: Thursday 05/06 afternoon PST works. Send a calendar invite for a 60-min deep-dive with Sergio and Jordan.

Thanks,
Arjun
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform
Skyline Health
arjun.patel@skylinehealth.com

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@skylinehealth.com>, Molly Chen <mchen@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Monitoring hooks & SDK architecture — follow-up + questions

Hi Arjun / Molly — thanks for the quick answers and the attached mapping. I've attached a short SDK quickstart (sdk_auth_quickstart.pdf) that includes a middleware snippet we recommend for Kong + Nodejs to propagate trace ids and attach latency headers. Snippets below for reference.

--- example middleware (Node/Express) ---
function redwoodTraceMiddleware(req, res, next) {
  const incoming = req.headers['x-request-id'] || req.headers['x-rw-trace-id'] || generateId();
  res.setHeader('X-RW-TRACE-ID', incoming);
  req.redwoodTrace = incoming;
  next();
}

// When calling Redwood API (from service that owns embeddings):
fetch('https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.RW_API_KEY}` ,
    'X-Request-Id': req.redwoodTrace
  },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
});

--- latency headers we will emit (examples) ---
- X-RW-CLIENT-LATENCY: time spent in request queue / client side
- X-RW-ROUTING-LATENCY: time in routing + gateway
- X-RW-MODEL-LATENCY: model compute time

On the signed-response question: we can include a lightweight HMAC header (x-rw-sig) that signs the response id + timestamp; we'll surface options in the deep-dive.

Proposed agenda for the 60-min deep-dive:
- 10m: current Skyline architecture + auth cadence
- 20m: SDK middleware + header mapping (trace headers and latency breakdown)
- 20m: embeddings / reranker data flow + signature proof options
- 10m: POC plan and success criteria (SLOs, dashboard joins)

I've tentatively scheduled Thu 2027-05-06 14:00 PST — I'll send a calendar invite. Sergio, Jordan — can you confirm you can drive the technical portion / POC support?

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
